title: This Fox Survived a Full Hour at Minus 80 Degrees Celsius

scenes.text: At minus seventy degrees Celsius, this fox is still fine.
Scientists once held an arctic fox at minus eighty for a full hour, and its body temperature didn't drop.
Its thick, layered coat holds in so much heat that it doesn't need to burn extra energy in normal winter cold.
A short muzzle and short legs lose even less heat to the air.
And less blood flows to its feet, so its toes don't freeze.
Minus eighty, and still going. A fox built for the coldest nights.

description:
An arctic fox was held at minus eighty degrees Celsius for an hour without its body temperature dropping.
Its layered coat, short legs and muzzle, and reduced blood flow to the feet keep the cold out.
Could you last a minute out there?
